confirmed: One Error mechanism for BOOT/Hardcore/Core/System/User Modules
CS input -> CSo OK, actual command response or ERROR
When CS fails, exactly one command+params entry in Log Buffer even mode off, no duplicate in cs/ac
When AC active, Error includes available actor identity irrespective of logging mode
Error owns Error Buffer; Logging owns Log Buffer; buffers independently retain last N or all when 0
CS has an INTERNAL typed OK/ERROR status; status is not guessed from raw CSo payload. Successful feedback is unwrapped and may literally equal ERROR or OK.
Presence of a returned value is separate from its contents; 0, false, null and empty string are valid payloads when explicitly present.
ERROR is ALWAYS a hard fail of the current execution; it must never be downgraded, marked recoverable, or reinterpreted as successful.
A canonical ERROR aborts the originating command/execution path and propagates failure; any whole-instance shutdown is governed by separate context-specific lifecycle rules.
